summary: Jacob Grimm was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Marburg (~1802–1805). He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1837) and Frederick William University Berlin (1841).
Jacob Holubeck is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2013).

Jacob N. Kinnard works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He has held academic posts at the College of William & Mary as Assistant Professor of Religion and at the Iliff School of Theology.

Religious studies scholar Jacob Neusner studied at Harvard, Lincoln College, Oxford, Columbia, and the Jewish Theological Seminary of America. He held posts at the University of South Florida (~1990–2000) and Bard College (~1994–2016), among others.

Jacob Samuel Speyer was an Indologist who studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern at Leiden University. He served as lecturer at the University of Amsterdam (1877–1889), professor of Latin at Groningen (1888–1903), and professor of Sanskrit at Leiden (1903–1913).

Jacob Wackernagel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Basel, Göttingen, Leipzig, and Oxford, under teachers including Friedrich Nietzsche and Theodor Benfey. He held chairs at the University of Basel (1879–1902, 1915–1936) and the University of Göttingen (1902–1915).

Jacqueline I. Stone is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD under William R. LaFleur at UCLA (~1983–1990) and served as a professor at Princeton University from 1990 to 2019.

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed doctoral studies under Julius Lipner. She has been affiliated with the University of Manchester, where she serves as an Honorary Research Fellow (attested 2026).

Jacques André was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris. He held academic posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

Jacques Bacot was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held teaching posts and a directorship of studies at the École Pratique des Hautes Études between 1919 and 1938.

Jacques Gernet was a scholar of sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE, and held professorships at the University of Paris (1959), EPHE (1955–1976), and the Collège de France (1975–1992).

Jacques Giès was a scholar of art history, sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate at Paris-Sorbonne University under Flora Blanchon. He taught at Paris-Sorbonne (1974–1998) and served as Chief Curator and later President of the Musée Guimet (2008–2011).

Jacques Leider is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at INALCO under Denise Bernot (~1992–1998). He taught at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999) before joining the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2001.
Jacques May was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as editor-in-chief of Hōbōgirin (~1965–1981) and as a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1968–1992).

Jacques Scheuer was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Université catholique de Louvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Madeleine Biardeau. He held posts at Université catholique de Louvain (~1978–2007) and KU Leuven (attested 2013).

Jacques Soustelle was a historian and anthropologist who studied under Marcel Mauss (~1930–1937) at the Faculty of Arts of Paris. He held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1951–1969) and the EHESS (~1969–1985).

Jadunath Sarkar was a historian who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He held teaching posts at Patna College (1899–1926) and Ravenshaw University, and served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).

Jagdish Kashyap was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied under Rahul Sankrityayan. He taught Pāli at Banaras Hindu University (~1940–1949) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1959–1965), and directed the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

Jaideva Singh was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Nankoo Bhaya Telang and Lakshman Joo. He served as chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (1973).

Jake H. Davis is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD from CUNY Graduate Center. He has held positions at Brown University (attested 2013–2018) and New York University.
